title: The nations allotted to angels, then given to Christ
source_text: Οὐδὲν δὲ θαυμαστὸν τὸ γενεαῖς τισι προφήτας γεγονέναι, ὑπερέχοντας ἐν τῇ παραδοχῇ τῆς θειότητος διὰ τὸν ἐπὶ πλεῖον εὔτονον καὶ ἐῤῥωμένον βίον ἑτέρων προφητῶν, τινῶν μὲν κατ᾿ αὐτοὺς ἄλλων δὲ προγενεστέρων ἢ μεταγενεστέρων. οὕτω δὲ οὐ θαυμαστὸν καί τινα καιρὸν γεγονέναι, ὅτ᾿ ἐξαίρετόν τι χρῆμα ἐπιδεδήμηκε τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ διαφέρον παρὰ τοὺς προγενεστέρους αὐτοῦ ἢ καὶ μεταγενεστέρους. ἔχει δέ τι ὁ περὶ τούτων λόγος μυστικώτερον καὶ βαθύτερον καὶ μὴ πάνυ τι φθάνειν δυνάμενον ἐπὶ τὴν δημωδεστέραν ἀκοήν. καὶ δεῖ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ταῦτα σαφηνισθῆναι καὶ ἀπαντηθῆναι πρὸς τὰ λεγόμενα περὶ τῆς Χριστοῦ ἐπιδημίας. ὅτι νῦν ἆρα μετὰ τοσοῦτον αἰῶνα ὁ θεὸς ἀνεμνήσθη δικαιῶσαι τὸ ἀνθρώπων γένος, πρότερον δὲ ἠμέλει; ἅψασθαι τοῦ περὶ μερίδων λόγου καὶ σαφηνίσαι. διὰ τί „ὅτε διεμέριζεν ὁ ὕψιστος ἔθνη. ὡς διέσπειρεν υἱοὺς Ἀδὰμ, ἔστησεν ὅρια ἐθνῶν κατ᾿ ἀριθμὸν ἀγγέλων θεοῦ· καὶ ἐγενήθη μερὶς κυρίου λαὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰακὼβ, σχοίνισμα κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ Ἰσραήλ“· καὶ δεήσει τὴν αἰτίαν εἰπεῖν τῆς εἰς ἕκαστον ὅριον γενέσεως ὑπὸ τὸν κεκληρωμένον τὸ ὅριον, καὶ πῶς εὐλόγως „ἐγενήθη μερὶς κυρίου λαὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰακὼβ, σχοίνισμα κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ Ἰσραήλ“· καὶ διὰ τί πρότερον μὲν ἦν „μερὶς κυρίου λαὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰακὼβ, σχοίνισμα κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ Ἰσραὴλ,“ περὶ δὲ τῶν ὕστερον λέγεται πρὸς τὸν σωτῆρα ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός· „αἴτησαι παρ᾿ ἐμοῦ, καὶ δώσω σοι ἔθνη τὴν κληρονομίαν σου καὶ τὴν κατάσχεσίν σου τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς.“ εἰσὶ γάρ τινες εἱρμοὶ καὶ ἀκολουθίαι ἄφατοι καὶ ἀνεκδιήγητοι περὶ τῆς κατὰ τὰς ἀνθρωπίνας ψυχὰς διαφόρου οἰκονομίας.
pass_a_gloss: Nothing wonderful (θαυμαστόν) that in some generations prophets have arisen, surpassing (ὑπερέχοντας) in the reception (παραδοχή) of divinity (θειότης), through their more vigorous (εὔτονον) and strong (ἐρρωμένον) life, other prophets, some contemporary with them, others earlier (προγενεστέρων) or later (μεταγενεστέρων). So too not wonderful that there was a certain time (καιρός) when some exceptional thing (ἐξαίρετόν τι χρῆμα) has sojourned (ἐπιδεδήμηκε) with the race of men, and differing from those before it or after. But the account (λόγος) about these has something more mystical (μυστικώτερον) and deeper (βαθύτερον), and not quite able to reach (φθάνειν) the more popular hearing (δημωδεστέραν ἀκοήν). And it is needed, for the sake of these being clarified (σαφηνισθῆναι) and of answering the things said about Christ's sojourn (ἐπιδημία) — 'so now after so great an age God remembered to set right the race (γένος) of men, but before neglected it?' — to touch on the account of portions (μερίδες) and clarify why 'when the Most High (ὕψιστος) divided (διεμέριζεν) nations, as he scattered (διέσπειρεν) sons of Adam, he set bounds (ὅρια) of nations according to the number of angels of God; and his people Jacob became the Lord's portion (μερίς), Israel the measured allotment (σχοίνισμα) of his inheritance (κληρονομία)'; and it will be needed to tell the cause (αἰτία) of the birth/coming-to-be (γένεσις) into each bound under the one allotted (κεκληρωμένον) the bound, and how reasonably (εὐλόγως) 'his people Jacob became the Lord's portion...'; and why before 'the Lord's portion was his people Jacob...', but about those later (τῶν ὕστερον) it is said to the Saviour by the Father: 'Ask (αἴτησαι) of me, and I will give you nations as your inheritance and as your possession (κατάσχεσις) the ends (πέρατα) of the earth.' For there are certain connections (εἱρμοί) and sequences (ἀκολουθίαι), unspeakable (ἄφατοι) and indescribable (ἀνεκδιήγητοι), about the differing economy/ordering (διάφορος οἰκονομία) concerning human souls.
pass_b_english: Nor is it any wonder that in certain generations there have been prophets who, through their more strenuous and vigorous lives, surpassed other prophets in receiving the divine, some of whom lived in their own time and others earlier or later. In the same way it is no wonder that there was also a certain time when something exceptional came to dwell among the human race, something that surpassed those who came before it, or even those after it. But the account of these matters holds something more mystical and deeper, which cannot easily reach the ears of the common crowd.

And to make these things clear, and to answer what is said about Christ’s coming, “So it is only now, after so long an age, that God has remembered to set the human race right, while before he did not care?”, we must touch on the doctrine of the portions and make clear why “when the Most High divided the nations, as he scattered the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the angels of God; and his people Jacob became the Lord’s portion, Israel the measured lot of his inheritance” (Deuteronomy 32:8–9). We shall need to state the reason for being born into each territory under the one to whom that territory was allotted, and how it was with good reason that “his people Jacob became the Lord’s portion, Israel the measured lot of his inheritance” (Deuteronomy 32:9); and why formerly “the Lord’s portion was his people Jacob, Israel the measured lot of his inheritance” (Deuteronomy 32:9), whereas of later times the Father says to the Saviour: “Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for your possession” (Psalm 2:8). For there are certain connections and sequences, unspeakable and beyond telling, in the varied ordering of human souls.

choices.term: διαφέρον παρὰ τοὺς προγενεστέρους ... ἢ καὶ μεταγενεστέρους
choices.choice: διαφέρον παρὰ τοὺς προγενεστέρους ... ἢ καὶ μεταγενεστέρους: 'stood apart from what came before it or after it' changed to 'surpassed those who came before it, or even those after it' (masculine plural; ἢ καί = 'or even')
opening καί: 'Yet' changed to 'And' (no contrast in the Greek)
inline (Deuteronomy 32:9) added to the third quotation of the verse, which had none
Deuteronomy 32:8–9 and Psalm 2:8 checked against LXX wording: correct

Deuteronomy 32:8–9 is quoted in the LXX form 'according to the number of the angels of God' (Hebrew text: 'sons of Israel'); this reading is the basis of Origen's doctrine of nations allotted to angels, so it is kept. σχοίνισμα (land measured out by rope) rendered 'measured lot'. ὅριον rendered 'boundaries' in the quotation and 'territory' in Origen's follow-up (εἰς ἕκαστον ὅριον γενέσεως ὑπὸ τὸν κεκληρωμένον τὸ ὅριον), which refers to the angel allotted each nation; γένεσις read as 'being born'. Psalm 2:8: LXX and English numbering agree. Celsus's question is re-quoted here with τὸ ἀνθρώπων γένος ('the human race') where 4.7 has τὸν ἀνθρώπων βίον ('human life'); each rendered as its own text has it. The third repetition of Deuteronomy 32:9 has ἦν ('was') instead of ἐγενήθη ('became'); rendered 'formerly ... was', and cited inline like the others (every quotation carries its reference). παρὰ τοὺς προγενεστέρους αὐτοῦ ἢ καὶ μεταγενεστέρους is masculine ('those who came before it, or even after it').
